items.notes: A narrated Wikipedia tutorial: page changes, menus and small interface text at 1280x1024. Human English captions exist on Commons (47 cues; the last cue's end is written 99:59:59, a useful sidecar case). Shows the narrator's own Wikipedia account and public user names. Commons refuses the tool (HTTP 429 to the neutral user agent, 2026-10-18): this item is pinned from a copy the maintainer downloads by hand (pin --from-file, against the Commons SHA-1) and fetched by every run from the test-media release.

items.title: After the lifting of the block: Case study of Turkey (Wikimania 2021)
items.author: Basak, Khutuck (Wikimania 2021; credit WMF)
items.attribution: "After the lifting of the block: Case study of Turkey" by Basak and Khutuck, Wikimania 2021, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
items.notes: A pre-recorded 19-minute conference talk by two speakers in Turkish-accented English, about 46 chunks. It opens with music and a title card: its captions put music from 8.2 s and the first words at 13.4 s, so the lead is non-speech rather than silence (to be labelled by listening). Its English captions look machine-made, so they are no reference transcript. A 480p transcode (29,909,095 bytes, no published checksum) is the lighter alternative. Commons refuses the tool (HTTP 429 to the neutral user agent, 2026-10-18): this item is pinned from a copy the maintainer downloads by hand (pin --from-file, against the Commons SHA-1) and fetched by every run from the test-media release.

items.title: Space Station Astronaut Discusses Record Breaking Mission with Previous Record Holder
items.author: NASA Johnson Space Center
items.attribution: "Space Station Astronaut Discusses Record Breaking Mission with Previous Record Holder" by NASA Johnson Space Center, public domain, via the Internet Archive
items.notes: The same recording as the Commons copy approved on 2026-10-18 (Commons refuses the tool): NASA Johnson's own public-affairs upload to the Internet Archive, whose caption file is identical to the NASA library's. A conversation between an astronaut on the station and a former record holder in Mission Control (NASA employees in their role), with the pauses of a space-to-ground link (the longest caption gaps 1.3 to 1.8 s), about 25 chunks. The item's creator field names a staff address, which is not repeated here.

media.video: VP9 854x480 (Commons transcode of a VP8 1920x1080 25 fps original)

items.notes: One speaker in German-accented English demonstrating a web tool, about 23 chunks. Commons has human-made English captions (205 cues), the best reference transcript of the set. The original is 254,967,178 bytes, so the 480p transcode is proposed; Commons publishes no checksum for transcodes, so source_checksum is the object store's ETag taken as the MD5 (unconfirmed until the pin) and the pin is otherwise trust on first use. Commons refuses the tool (HTTP 429 to the neutral user agent, 2026-10-18): this item is pinned from a copy the maintainer downloads by hand (pin --from-file, against the Commons SHA-1) and fetched by every run from the test-media release. A hand-downloaded transcode has no published SHA-1; its ETag is recorded as the MD5 to compare.

items.title: NASA's SpaceX Crew-8 Crew Arrival at Kennedy Space Center (25 February 2024)
items.author: NASA (video: Ben Smegelsky)
items.attribution: "NASA's SpaceX Crew-8 Crew Arrival" by NASA/Ben Smegelsky, public domain, via the NASA Image and Video Library
items.notes: Chosen on 2026-10-19 under the maintainer's go for public, freely licensed items of the design's shapes. The crew's arrival at the runway and their remarks outdoors, 28 minutes: the first caption is at 5:17, so about five minutes of arrival with no speech (aircraft and wind noise, to be heard) come before the first word. NASA publishes no checksum: the pin is trust on first use over HTTPS, cross-checked by a second, hosted fetch. NASA media carries no endorsement. Looked at on 2026-10-19 (sixteen frames): the crew, NASA officials at a lectern and the aircraft; no member of the public is shown.

items.title: How to Create a Map from a Table Using data.census.gov (U.S. Census Bureau, 2022)
items.author: U.S. Census Bureau
items.attribution: "How to Create a Map from a Table Using data.census.gov" by the U.S. Census Bureau, public domain (a US government work), via the Internet Archive
items.notes: Chosen on 2026-10-19 under the maintainer's go. A narrated screen recording of the Census Bureau's data site: a table of county figures is opened, filtered and mapped, with small interface text and numbers. A US government work; the Internet Archive copy is a mirror of the Bureau's own channel made by an archive user, which the go allows for government works. The licence rests on 17 U.S.C. 105: no Census page states it for this file. Looked at on 2026-10-19 (nine frames): the presenter (Census Bureau staff, named on screen in her role), then the site; the video carries burned-in captions, on-screen text that matches the speech. No private person's data is shown.
